title: Profile summary
text: Jof Davies builds and runs the systems a business depends on: CRM, customer data, email infrastructure, integrations between platforms and, since 2025, AI-driven automation. At MTDCNC he has owned the CRM and marketing systems end to end since June 2016 and has built a set of agent pipelines in Claude Code and Python that read a shared inbox, run a task board, publish content and drive a video-edit pipeline, all behind spend caps and human release gates. Before that he ran his own consultancy migrating CRMs for UK insurance brokers, and earlier replaced spreadsheet processes with Access and VBA systems. He is hands-on, documents what he builds and trains the people who use it.

title: The role Jof is looking for
text: Jof is looking for a permanent, full-time role where the main work is business systems, CRM and marketing-operations systems, integration, data, or AI workflow automation. Typical titles that fit: Business Systems Manager or Analyst, CRM Manager or Developer, Marketing Automation or Marketing Operations Manager, RevOps or GTM systems roles, AI Automation Specialist or Engineer, Automation Manager, Integration Specialist. He wants to keep doing the kind of work he does now at MTDCNC: finding manual work, modelling the data and building the automation. He is not looking for a marketing manager or content role, and he is not looking for contract or freelance work because he wants a permanent position.

text: Jof lives in Northampton, UK, and has a full UK driving licence. He has the right to work in the UK. He prefers hybrid working within commuting distance of Northampton, with two or three days a week in the office, and is equally open to fully remote roles based in the UK. Occasional travel, including a couple of days a month in London, is fine. His notice period is three months. Salary expectations are discussed directly with Jof rather than quoted by the assistant. The quickest way to reach him is the contact form on jofdavies.com or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/joffad.

Not used in production: n8n, Make, Power Automate, UiPath, Workato, Kubernetes and Azure. He builds the same kinds of workflow automation in Python, Zapier and Google Apps Script, and he learns new platforms quickly, but he would say so plainly rather than list them as skills. text: Jof writes and maintains Python, SQL, JavaScript, VBA and some PHP, and has done since building Access and VBA systems in 2007. His job titles have been in systems, data and marketing rather than software engineering. Since 2025 most of his new code is written with AI-assisted development in Claude Code: he specifies the work, directs the agent, reviews and tests the output, and owns the result in production. He is clear that this is AI-assisted development and not unaided software engineering. What he brings to it is judgement about what to build, how to control it and how to keep it running: spend caps, release gates, handover documents and operations plans.

title: MTDCNC: role overview (June 2016 to present)
text: Jof has worked at MTDCNC in Northampton since June 2016. MTDCNC is a B2B media business serving the manufacturing technology sector. His title is Digital Marketing Manager, with responsibility for CRM, systems and automation. He is the sole owner of the CRM (more than 20,000 contacts), the email infrastructure and the marketing systems, across more than 50 client accounts. Over ten years the role has covered CRM architecture and automation, Python data tooling, platform integrations, email development and deliverability, a global media ingest and archive system, video production and livestream engineering, staff training and, since 2025, a programme of AI agent pipelines.

title: AI agent pipelines built in 2025 and 2026
text: In 2025 and 2026 Jof built and now runs a set of AI agent pipelines at MTDCNC using Claude Code and Python. They are: an inbox agent that reads a shared mailbox, extracts tasks and posts them to Monday.com with a 07:00 daily brief; a board watcher that executes tagged tasks and reports back; a tool that turns a magazine PDF into categorised, illustrated web posts through the WordPress REST API; a two-voice podcast generator using Gemini text-to-speech; a deliverability tracker; and a dispatcher that drives a video-edit pipeline in Adobe Premiere. Every pipeline that can spend money runs behind a spend ledger, a canary and a kill switch, and nothing is sent or published without a person releasing it.

title: Inbox agent: a mailbox turned into a task list
text: The inbox agent is built in Claude Code and Python. It reads a mailbox's inbox and sent items since its last run, discards notifications, promotions and junk, and extracts the real tasks. Each task is checked against the open items on a Monday.com task board: new tasks are added with a note of the source email, and existing items have their status moved when the mail shows progress. Where it can do the groundwork alone it does, for example looking something up, drafting a reply or a report and posting what it found on the item. At 07:00 each day it posts a brief grouped by whose move each task is, in deadline order. It runs under a daily spend cap of a few pounds and it prepares drafts but never sends them: a named person releases anything that goes out.

title: Task-board watcher: tags fire tools
text: The board watcher is the second of Jof's agents at MTDCNC. It watches a Monday.com task board. When someone tags the agent on an item, it works out which tool the request needs, such as a report, a draft or a data check, runs it, writes the result back to the item and mentions the person who asked. Items are closed on evidence that the work is done, not on an instruction alone. Replies and drafts it prepares wait for a person to release them. It is built in Claude Code and Python and uses the Monday.com API.

title: How Jof controls AI automation: spend caps and human release
text: Jof's rule for AI automation is that it must be safe to leave running. Every pipeline that can spend money has four controls: a ledger that records what each run costs, a hard cap it cannot exceed, a canary run on a small sample before any batch, and a kill switch that stops it at once. Large jobs are chunked so a failure costs little. Separately, the tools prepare and a person releases: emails, messages and published content wait as drafts until a named person lets them go. Steps that do not need judgement are written as plain Python with no model calls, which makes them cheaper and repeatable. Each system has a handover document and an operations plan so that other people can run it.

title: Magazine PDF to WordPress posts
text: Jof built a Python tool that takes each issue of MTDCNC's bi-monthly magazine as a PDF and publishes its articles to the website. It splits the issue into articles of a page or longer, extracts the text and images, takes the category from the page label and sets the right company as author. It writes a preview folder first so the result can be checked, then creates the posts through the WordPress REST API with images placed inline. He built it with AI-assisted development, but it runs as plain Python with no model calls, so an issue costs nothing to process and the output is repeatable. A companion tool draws the mock-up images of each new issue from scratch for use on the website and in emails.

title: Two-voice podcast generator
text: Jof built a tool that turns a written findings document into a two-voice podcast episode, in which a host interviews an analyst and the episode ends with calls to action. It uses Gemini text-to-speech and runs behind a hard-capped spend ledger. He also built a tool that combines the mastered tracks of the audio edition of the magazine into one file with chapter markers and writes the episode description, ready for upload to a podcast platform.

title: Video-edit pipeline dispatcher
text: Jof designed and documented a dispatcher that runs a video-edit pipeline unattended. It picks edit jobs from a queue, restores any archived material, opens Adobe Premiere itself and builds sequences from XML to the house cutting rules, such as minimum shot lengths and where a cut may fall. The deliverable is a real Premiere project that an editor opens and finishes. Idle jobs are archived to QNAP network storage and restored before a run. If the machine faults, the job is held rather than lost and the operator is paged through Pushover. Source footage is never moved or deleted by the tool. The pipeline has been handed over to a permanent runner machine with a written operations plan and a fault-recovery procedure.

title: CRM automation in GoHighLevel
text: At MTDCNC Jof designed and built a multi-branch lead qualification workflow in the GoHighLevel CRM. It covers intake validation, enrichment, conditional branching, a sequence of HTML and plain-text follow-up emails driven by how each contact engages, lead scoring, notifications to sales staff and updates to CRM state. He also designed the CRM's structure, tagging and reporting, and earlier ran the company's CRM on FiveCRM. He has working knowledge of HubSpot but GoHighLevel is the platform he has built the most in. A large deep-zoom diagram of the workflow is on the workflow automation profile page of jofdavies.com.

title: Python CRM import validator
text: Jof wrote a Python import validator that stops bad or duplicate records entering the CRM. Each incoming record runs down a resolution chain: match on email, then exact name, then company domain, then fuzzy name matching using rapidfuzz. Fuzzy matches of 90% or more are approved automatically. Matches of 75 to 89% go to a review queue, together with any record whose country does not agree with the one on file. The tool writes an Excel review workbook so a person can decide the uncertain cases quickly. Only resolved records reach the CRM.

title: Bot-click filter for campaign statistics
text: Security scanners and mail privacy proxies open emails and click links automatically, which inflates campaign statistics. Jof built a Python bot-click filter that classifies each click using Apple Mail Privacy Protection address ranges, an IP classification cache held in SQLite and behavioural scoring. Campaign reports then show activity from real people rather than scanners, which makes the engagement figures given to clients honest.

title: Campaign reporting and the 121,663-contact master list
text: Jof generates client campaign reports by script, reading the email platform's production MySQL database directly and read-only, and writing an Excel report with a summary, opens and clicks. Any write to that database follows a plan, apply, verify routine. In October 2026 he merged the contact bases of two systems into a single deduplicated master list of 121,663 contacts. He also built deduplication tooling between the CRM and the email platform.

title: Integrations built at MTDCNC
text: Integrations Jof has built at MTDCNC include: Monday.com with Google Apps Script, pulling YouTube statistics into boards; Zapier with webhooks, taking LinkedIn posts through Google Sheets and an AI rewrite into WordPress; a Flask application on Render that uploads to YouTube using OAuth 2.0; a Node and Express proxy that makes Monday.com images public so Zapier can use them; WordPress REST API publishing; read-only reporting from a MySQL production database; the Dropbox team API; Pushover notifications; and the Gemini API for text-to-speech. He works with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth 2.0 and JSON routinely.

title: LinkedIn to WordPress automation
text: Jof built an automation that turns LinkedIn posts into website articles using Zapier, webhooks, Google Sheets, Formatter steps and an AI rewrite. Post URLs are collected into Google Sheets with Phantombuster, then cleaned and validated. Webhooks extract the body text and media of each post. The content is rewritten into an editorial-style article by an AI model, and the image and article are posted to WordPress. The spreadsheet is updated with status and metadata, and fallback logic handles failed rewrites and republished posts. A deep-zoom diagram of the workflow is on the workflow automation profile page of the site.

title: YouTube publishing automation (Ultimate Video Uploader)
text: Jof built a YouTube publishing automation known internally as the Ultimate Video Uploader. A trigger on the project management board starts it. It formats titles, descriptions, tags and categories, handles thumbnails, branches on whether a video is short-form (under two minutes) or long-form, uploads and schedules through the YouTube API, publishes to WordPress, logs status and notifies people on success or failure. It turned a multi-person publishing routine into a single button. Related code is in his GitHub repositories, including a Flask YouTube uploader deployed on Render.

title: Email infrastructure and deliverability
text: Jof runs MTDCNC's email infrastructure, which has carried around one million emails a month at peak through SendGrid and Mailwizz. He maintains SPF, DKIM and DMARC across the sending domains, monitors sender reputation and blacklists, and manages suppression and unsubscribes. He has hand-coded more than 3,000 HTML and VML email campaigns that render correctly across Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail. He built a deliverability tracker that follows authentication and reputation for each sending brand. He has also used Mailchimp and ActiveCampaign.

title: Email build standard: rule set, linter and converters
text: Jof wrote the rule set that MTDCNC's emails are built to, covering Outlook's VML rendering, DPI scaling and dark mode, and a Python linter called email_lint that every build must pass before it is proofed. He built a Python pipeline from Photoshop design to HTML, and a converter that brings supplied or AI-generated HTML up to the house standard, extracting and compressing images and rendering the result at desktop and phone width. Test sends go to test lists; live campaigns are prepared as drafts and sent by a person.

title: Global video ingest, proxy and archive system
text: Jof designed and deployed MTDCNC's media ingest and archive system. Two QNAP storage units of about 100 TB each sit on site and at a remote location. The office unit synchronises with Dropbox so footage can be ingested from anywhere, with fast local access over a 10 Gb network and a 1 Gb leased line. Footage replicates hourly, proxy files are generated automatically at about 5% of the original size so remote editors can start work on slow connections, and new material is archived nightly to AWS S3 Glacier. About 100 TB is archived at roughly £100 a month. The system cost about £7,000 in hardware with no software licences and serves around 20 remote editors in the UK, Europe, the USA, Mexico and India. Commercial platforms he evaluated were quoted in the tens of thousands of pounds a year.

title: Automated proxy generation
text: Proxy creation in MTDCNC's media system is automated with HBBatchBeast and a custom HandBrake preset that Jof tuned. A workstation checks the project footage folder every hour and processes only new files. The preset keeps enough picture quality for editing, cuts file size substantially for remote transfer, standardises the format for every editor and decodes predictably in Premiere Pro. This removed manual transcoding and means editors usually have proxy-ready footage within about an hour of upload.

title: How jofdavies.com and this chatbot were built
text: jofdavies.com is Jof's personal project. It is a static site of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework and no build step, deployed from GitHub to Cloudflare Pages. A Cloudflare Worker handles the chatbot and the contact form. The chatbot uses retrieval: a curated library of short records about Jof's roles, projects and tools is embedded with OpenAI embeddings and stored in Cloudflare Vectorize. For each question the Worker retrieves the closest records and asks the model to answer only from them. Writing to the library requires a secret key, and questions are rate-limited and capped per day. The contact form sends email through Postmark. Workflow diagrams use OpenSeadragon deep zoom. Jof built it with AI-assisted development in VS Code and rebuilt it in November 2026.
